Several named evidence strips no longer show the named action at their sampled center: generation_and_compute_pair shows ONE CABLE ASHORE, estimate_dial_rises shows the route split, and customer_chair_stays_empty shows the FERC notice. That weakens confidence in exact VO-to-action timing even though caption-to-voice sync passes.

The registered-motion report remains below its 1.2% reference floor in many shot samples; the film is alive through distributed ambient regions and event bursts more than through consistently strong hero-object performance.
Compared with the r9 anchor contact sheet, several current diagrams and lock/cable motifs have limited contact shadow, material articulation, and depth separation within the flat-vector style.
The square poster leaves a clipped fragment of the persistent proposal pill touching the top edge, which reads as an avoidable crop/tangent.
Only 25 of 35 planned SFX events are verified audible. Every shot is sonified and the gate passes, but ten planned accents do not produce a measurable lift.
The living-screen report identifies quiet two-second windows at 60s and 64s, plus static outro windows from 120s through 126s.
strengths: The current objective gate passes at 10.0: sharpness, HUD and caption clarity, event cadence, beat density, scene structure, camera motion, caption sync, music, SFX coverage, silence dip, living-screen coverage, hook motion, and first-frame contrast all clear their thresholds.
The first half-second now contains a visible plug-and-hive action, and the opening socket question pays off through the one-inch-short and Alaska-value socket imagery.
The marine-blue, chartreuse, coral, and cream-paper palette is story-motivated and visibly distinct from the gray industrial r9 anchor world.

Proposal status remains explicit throughout, while the narrative fairly distinguishes primary data-center use, conditional Railbelt power, missing proof, study priority, and lack of construction authority.

All fourteen claims map to primary FERC materials; the film and post avoid converting the 100 MW estimate into demonstrated output or promising customer, financing, construction, grid, economic, or environmental outcomes.
The post has a strong LinkedIn hook, specific figures, a balanced pro-test position, a real closing question, and passes its caption gate with a 9.2 score.
Reported audio measures I=-14.45 LUFS, TP=-2.44 dBTP, and LRA=6.8 LU; sourced music is credited by track, composer, site, and CC BY 4.0 license. This is report-based, not a human-listening claim.

Typography and captions rise from my prior 5.0 to 7.6 because the film changed, not my standard: the visible "100 MW s." typo is now "100 MW.", the broken "P"/"M" cue split is now "PM" within one cue, and the current caption clarity and synchronization gates pass.
